text:
MIN arrives in Calgary on a one-night turnaround from a 4-3 overtime loss at EDM, where Evan Bouchard ended it. The Wild are 3-1-1 in their last five and without Olli Maatta, Jared Spurgeon and Marcus Foligno. With Spurgeon out, Jonas Brodin has moved in beside Quinn Hughes, and David Spacek and Daemon Hunt are both playing more. CGY, rested after beating CAR 3-2 four days ago to end the Hurricanes' seven-game winning streak, is 2-3-0 in its last five and missing Samuel Honzek. There's a reunion in it too: Blake Coleman returns to Calgary for the first time since leaving, and Jake Middleton meets the Wild for the first time.

The Flames' record is worse than their play. They have taken 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, against 53% for MIN. They also take 4.8 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opposing power plays. In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt has saved 6.9 goals more than expected this season. Projected Flames starter Dustin Wolf is 8.0 goals worse than expected, and last season ended at -2.8 against Wallstedt's +5.8.

Kirill Kaprizov carries a seven-game point streak and is 53% to score and 81% for a point tonight. Matt Boldy, on the top power play, is 48% to score. Hughes sits two points from 500 career points. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Joel Eriksson Ek, 61% for a point, above his season pace because his line creates chances. For CGY, Matt Coronato leads the power play.
